scorecard.rationale: The uncontrolled 14-person Parkinson brewed-green-tea pilot reports mean fatigue rising from 28.4 to 32.1, with higher medians in the same cohort and no paired variance or exact fatigue p value. Opposing evidence includes a postoperative brewed-tea comparison and customary relief of tiredness. Some isolated caffeine or caffeine-theanine tasks favored less fatigue. The newly verified usual-diet cycling studies saw mixed descriptive estimates and no treatment effect on perceived exertional fatigue. Extra exercise and constituent data address different settings and preparations. The closest Parkinson observation retains tentative worsening. Controlled brewed-tea Parkinson data and the remaining original measures are open.
